01 of 04

CIS statement pipeline and dashboards

Staff see, for every client, which contractor tax statements are still missing, without checking by hand.

Status
Live: intake, matching, filing and client dashboards; statement requests in first use
Stack
Python, PostgreSQL, Self-hosted OCR, OpenAI, n8n
Role
Designed and built
  • 41client dashboardsat launch, Aug 20261
  • 335 of 351documents received since July with a final outcome22 Jul to 13 Oct 2026, WhatsApp and email, Oct 20262

What it does

  • Clients

    • Send statements by WhatsApp or email, as a photo, PDF or spreadsheet.
    • Get a WhatsApp request in English or Georgian naming each contractor's missing months.

  • Staff

    • Pull every client's expected deductions from QuickBooks after one attended two-factor login.
    • See each client's missing statements, their QuickBooks value and whether we asked.
    • Open any statement, renamed and filed by client, from the hub, PC or web.
    • Correct any expected figure; an append-only ledger records who, when and why.

Problem

Construction subcontractors have tax deducted by every contractor they work for, and claiming it back needs a statement from each contractor for each month. The statements arrived scattered over WhatsApp and email and were reconciled once a year by hand, so discrepancies surfaced only at year end and delayed clients' repayment claims.

What I built

A pipeline built to run each quarter, with the first quarter complete. It starts from the accounting system's expected deductions, then reads every statement that arrives, matches it to its expected month and files it, holding anything unclear for a person. Staff track every client on one dashboard.

Under the hood

  • Nothing is dropped: every document that arrives gets a recorded outcome, from matched to held for a person.
  • A statement is filed only when client, contractor and month are all certain; the sender's identity is used only to break a tie.
  • OCR runs on the firm's own machine, so no page image goes to a cloud OCR service. An LLM reads the extracted text and a rules check re-reads month and amount; where they disagree, the rules win on a known contractor layout, otherwise the document is held.
  • Regression set: after each fix to the reader, 477 real documents are read again and compared with a person's recorded answers.
  • Scheduled checks run on live data: weekly invariants, a heartbeat per job and a contradiction check of every published page.
  • Databases and stored files are backed up nightly, encrypted; a rehearsed restore in October matched every count.
  • Python and PostgreSQL, money as exact decimals, 4,2938 automated tests; a snapshot test fails if a change alters a client's own page, which is built without firm-wide data.

Results

  • 62 of 649 Q1 2026-27 statements identified were matched to what each client owed.
  • 1710 duplicate copies caught by file fingerprint and counted once.
  • QuickBooks export: about 4 minutes of manual download per company before, now under a minute11.

Decisions and trade-offs

  • Hold rather than guess: more documents wait for a person, but no wrong match reaches a client's folder.
  • Statement requests are attended: each client's expected list is approved and checked first, and a person confirms each send, one client at a time. It costs staff time, but a wrong or repeated message cannot reach a client.
  • Each request names every contractor and only the periods still missing, for example "Marlowe Groundworks: 6 April to 5 May" (a made-up name). Messages run longer, but a client asked for one contractor by name had re-sent statements we already held.

02 of 04

AI chatbot on WhatsApp and the website, with a team dashboard

Clients get answers on WhatsApp and the website; staff step in from one dashboard.

Status
Live; one firm in production
Stack
TypeScript, Supabase, n8n, WhatsApp Cloud API, OpenAI, Anthropic
Role
Designed and built
  • 42 of 42acceptance benchmark cases passedlive AI model, Jul 20263

What it does

  • Clients

    • Ask questions on WhatsApp or the website chat in 612 languages.
    • Ask what we still need; staff check and reply, so the bot never guesses.
    • Register for CIS (construction tax) or a taxpayer reference in website chat, uploading ID.
    • Send several files on WhatsApp and get one reply confirming how many arrived.

  • Staff

    • Take over any thread and reply under their own name; the bot goes silent.
    • Send messages and files; after WhatsApp's 24-hour reply window, approved templates only.
    • See each statement request we sent, labelled in the client's WhatsApp thread.

  • Admins

    • Check company filing deadlines, pull a client's files and set reminders by WhatsApp command.

Problem

Clients would rather ask a question or send a photo on WhatsApp than write an email, and the construction tax (CIS) statement pipeline needed a client-facing channel where clients already are. A growing office cannot answer every message quickly and consistently, and a wrong tax rate or another client's details in a reply is a real risk.

What I built

An LLM assistant that answers clients on WhatsApp and the firm's website chat. It is also the client-facing front end of the CIS statement pipeline: files sent to the WhatsApp number are queued for the pipeline, confirmed with one reply, and alerted to staff if one fails to save. Staff read every thread on a team dashboard and can take any of them over.

Under the hood

  • The model is instructed to answer only from the firm's service material, and code checks every reply for prices, tax rates, formatting and confidentiality before it is sent.
  • An evaluation set of 4913 scripted client conversations, 26 of which must pass on every run, goes through the bot's real reply route against the live model.
  • The main reply call has a timeout, two retries and a circuit breaker, then fails over to a second AI provider.
  • Spending caps per firm and per user, and a per-user rate limit, stop a fault or misuse from running up AI costs.
  • The bot masks common UK identifiers in each new message and in stored memory lines.
  • An hourly sync copies a short record per client from the CIS pipeline into the bot's own database, with no money fields; the bot never reads the CIS database.
  • TypeScript on Supabase, with n8n carrying every WhatsApp message in and out; 1,68914 automated tests.

Decisions and trade-offs

  • Redirect, never guess: tax-rate questions always get a GOV.UK link set in code, and a client can ask for a person at any point. The bot answers fewer questions on its own, but no client gets a guessed rate.
  • Unattended messages are pre-approved templates only, each checked for duplicates, opt-outs, deletion requests and business hours, and a blocked send is logged with its reason. Reminders are less flexible, but no free text reaches a client without a person.
  • Confidentiality is enforced after generation: a reply that names a company not recorded against the sender is replaced by a refusal. It can refuse a safe answer, and refuses in English only so far, but a reply naming another client's company does not go out.

Debugging story

A client sent eight photos at once and only some were stored. Each new file was first saved under the same placeholder name, which the database accepts only once, so photos arriving together were rejected. Each file now gets its own placeholder; a test reproduces the loss, and a live burst test after the fix stored 8 of 815 photos, each paired to its message.

03 of 04

Making Tax Digital figures from bank statements

Turns a sole trader's bank statements into checked figures for their quarterly tax update.

Status
In internal use for quarterly Making Tax Digital submissions
Stack
Python, PDF text parsing, Rules engine
Role
Designed and built
  • 140 of 140real statements self-verified14,801 transactions, 0 parse failures, Jul 20264
  • 9bank statement layouts read11 UK bank brands, 10 tested on real statements, Aug 20265

What it does

  • Accountant

    • Load a client's PDF statements; any that fail the bank's own totals are refused.
    • Review every uncertain line in one list before it counts towards a figure.
    • Answer grouped questions on uncertain lines, largest amounts first, before saving a rule. built, not in daily use yet
    • Set rules for one client or a whole trade; client rules override trade rules.
    • Get the self-employment return boxes (SA103), a review workbook and the filing spreadsheet.

Problem

Making Tax Digital asks sole traders for quarterly figures, and each quarter starts from bank statements whose every line must be read, classed as income or expense and totalled. By hand it takes a long time, and external tools cost too much for the work to pay. One misread or misclassified line also changes the figure that gets filed.

What I built

A local tool that parses each bank's PDF statements, verifies them against the bank's own totals and classifies every line with layered fixed rules. A person always reviews and files; the tool sends nothing to HMRC.

Under the hood

  • A statement is trusted only when its lines re-add to the bank's printed totals and running balance to the penny; a balance break is shown at its row.
  • No AI and no network calls in reading or sorting; an automated check blocks common network and AI libraries.
  • Rules sit in three layers, client over trade over firm, and one client can switch off a trade rule without touching anyone else.
  • Money is held as exact decimals, never floating point, and the tool never modifies a statement file.
  • Python, with lint, strict type checks and 97616 automated tests.

Results

  • A rule change meant for one client would have moved a figure on another client's filed return. A regression test pinning a sample client's return boxes to the penny caught it before it landed.
  • After rules were reordered, cash taken out at a supermarket cashpoint was about to count as a claimable meal cost. An automated test caught it before any return was filed.

Decisions and trade-offs

  • Fixed rules, no AI: the same statements and rules always give the same figures, and every category traces back to a rule. A new client means more questions for the accountant at first, but no figure moves without a reason.
  • Read the text layer the PDF already holds, not a picture of the page. Scanned statements are refused for now, but every amount is taken as the bank printed it, and the totals check proves it.
  • Local and single user: the page answers only on the same computer and has no login, so one person uses it today. A hosted version for more staff waits until it has proved itself on real quarters.

04 of 04

Business automations in n8n

Client messages, documents, registrations and filing deadlines are handled in the background; staff are told what needs them.

Status
Live
Stack
n8n, WhatsApp Cloud API, Microsoft Graph, Companies House API, Supabase
Role
Designed and built
  • 14active workflowslive n8n instance, Oct 20266

What it does

  • Staff

    • Get WhatsApp and email reminders before Companies House filing deadlines, and when overdue.
    • Work from a deadline tracker refreshed from Companies House every day.
    • Receive a WhatsApp alert with folder link and photo count per website registration.
    • Get an alert when a filing step fails, saying what to file by hand.

Problem

Client work arrives on WhatsApp, by email and through a website form, and every client company has Companies House filing deadlines. Done by hand it is slow, and a dropped step or a missed deadline goes unnoticed until it is late.

What I built

Background workflows in n8n. The 1417 active workflows, by job:

  • Messages in 2 workflows

    WhatsApp text goes to the chatbot, files to the document pipeline; an older email route runs only when started by hand.

  • Messages out 2 workflows

    Template messages leave through two guarded send workflows: client messages from the firm's apps, and document filing alerts to staff.

  • Document filing 3 workflows

    Each read document is filed in the right client folder in cloud storage; two helpers clear stale copies and empty folders.

  • Registrations 1 workflow

    Each website registration becomes a client folder with its ID photos and a details file.

  • Compliance 5 workflows

    Two daily trackers check Companies House and remind staff, one daily sync feeds the team dashboard, two refresh rows on request.

  • Monitoring 1 workflow

    A 30-minute check emails the owner once when the chatbot's client records go stale, again as a reminder, and on recovery.

Also built, now switched off: the chatbot's first version, which searched FAQs and HMRC guidance and drafted answers with an AI model. It never answered a client.

Under the hood

  • Every webhook the firm's own apps call checks a shared secret or token, and no credentials are stored in the workflow files.
  • Reminder sends from the firm's apps reserve a one-time idempotency key before sending, so a duplicate is refused, and make up to 3 attempts.
  • Incoming WhatsApp files are checked against allowed types and de-duplicated on the provider's message id before they are queued.
  • Only approved templates go out and blank fields are refused; filing retries before alerting staff, and a folder is deleted only when it is empty.

Decisions and trade-offs

  • Template messages leave through two send workflows, not from each app. It adds a hop, but the secret check and the template allow-list sit in the send workflows instead of in every app.
  • A failed WhatsApp reply cannot block a document from being saved: the two run separately. A client may wait for an answer, but no file is lost.
  • The live workflows are exported to git, so changes can be reviewed outside n8n. The exports are only as current as the last export, but a broken edit can be compared with the last good copy.

How I work

Every system starts from a written spec: what it does, what it must never do, and how we will know it works. A person signs off every figure before it is filed and every statement request before it is sent. Each system ships with handover documents, so someone else can run it.

I build with AI coding tools. Tests are written first and seen failing, and a second AI reviews each piece of work before it merges. What I own is the problem framing, the design and its safeguards, checking the results, and running the systems live.

Background

AI and Automation Specialist at Trusted Figures, a London accountancy firm. I started with simple scripts and n8n workflows in 2025. Production systems followed from February 2026, starting with a compliance tracker, and the WhatsApp assistant and the construction tax (CIS) statement pipeline from April 2026.

Languages: English, Georgian, Russian, Greek.
